The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

In Active voice (look at the options), it should be in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

"By whom?" is changed into "Who" while transforming from Passive to Active.

For example:

By whom are you taught Math? (or) Who are you taught Math by? (Passive)

Who teaches you Math? (Active)

"Who" is changed into "Whom" while transforming from Passive to Active.

For example:

Who is being taught by you? (Passive)

Whom are you teaching? (Active)

The sentence in the Passive voice is in past indefinite tense. So, the sentence in the Active voice should be in past indefinite tense.

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (d)

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the positive degree of comparison:

This is the largest tree in the park.
options_en: No other tree in the park is as large as this one.
This tree is the largest in the park.
The largest tree in the park is this one.
In the park, this tree is larger than other trees.
questions.solution_en:
The original sentence, "This is the largest tree in the park," is in the superlative degree of comparison. To transform it into a positive degree, we must ensure the sentence uses "as...as" to indicate comparison without implying comparative or superlative status.

Option a) is correct. It uses the positive degree ("as large as") and compares this tree to other trees in the park without explicitly stating it is the largest.

Options b) and c) are in the superlative degrees, while option d) is in the comparative degree.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Sentence C provides more details about pickpocketing, describing where it commonly occurs: crowded places like markets, public transportation, or tourist areas. This sentence logically follows the introduction in B, as it adds more context about the locations where pickpocketing happens.

Therefore, the correct order is BCA

Hence, option (b) is correct.

"All bark and no bite" describes someone who makes a lot of noise or gives the appearance of being active or threatening, but in reality, they do nothing significant or don't follow through.

"The ball is in your court" means that it is now your responsibility to take action or make a decision.

"Don't bite the hand that feeds you" means that you shouldn't harm or be ungrateful toward someone who is helping or supporting you.

"Let sleeping dogs lie" means that it's best to avoid interfering with something that is currently at rest or causing no trouble.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

After we come to power at the Centre, we will conduct a countrywide caste census.
options_en: A countrywide caste census should be conducted by us when we come to power at the Centre.
A countrywide caste census will have been conducted by us after we come to power at the Centre.
A countrywide caste census will be conducted by us as and when we come to power at the Centre.
A countrywide caste census will be conducted by us after we come to power at the Centre.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb ['have been' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive. In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Par- the face value of a share or other security, as distinct from its market value.

Pare- trim (something) by cutting away its outer edges.

Pear- a yellowish- or brownish-green edible fruit

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).
